text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has directed the law ministry to make legal provisions under which negligence on the part of police officials or doctors in handling accident cases which often result in loss of life should be treated as murder.

- The actual gross domestic product growth rate during the first ten months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) is estimated at three percent with agriculture growing four percent, no growth in large-scale manufacturing and services growing four percent.
- Indian foreign ministry officials told reporters the prime ministers of Pakistan and India would hold their first meeting in eight years on May 12.
- A proposed $2.5 billion gas pipeline transiting embattled Afghanistan is edging closer to reality with the announcement of an imminent go-ahead by an Argentine-led consortium.
- Pakistan is likely to finalise a $400 million Asian Development Bank loan agreement for financial sector reform some time in September-October this year.
- The Farmers Associates Pakistan has opposed importing cotton from India in the presence of two million cotton bales stocked with cotton factories.

- Exporters in the first meeting of the Export Development Committee on Wednesday are expected to ask for more funds under the concessionary export refinance scheme from the present level of 35 billion rupees a year to 75 billion rupees a year.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has permitted overseas investors to buy bonds and other fixed-income certificates and has abolished witholding tax on the return on capital gains against such investments.
- To avoid wheat shortages the government has decided to involve the private sector in the import of wheat.
- The government will suffer an immediate loss of about 200 million rupees if it goes ahead with the proposed withdrawal of customs duty on import of sugar.
- Communications Minister Azam Khan Hoti told the National Assembly that Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd will only be privatised when its finances are in order.
- The Privatisation Commission is looking for an experienced instituion to act as financial adviser for the sale of the government's stake in Allied Bank Ltd.
- Morocco's phosphate gaint Office Cherifien des Phosphate and Pakistan Al-Noor firm signed a $220 million joint-venture deal to build a fertiliser complex in Karachi.
- Pakistan is expected to buy up to 50 percent less fuel oil and diesel during July-September compared to its second quarter imports because of the monsoon season.
- Pakistan will receive offers for its approximately 330,000-tonne soft white wheat tender on Tuesday.
THE NEWS
- Fifteen religious and sectarian parties agreed to observe a seven-point code of conduct to promote religious harmony at a meeting with Punjab provincial government officials in Lahore.
- The government has identified 13 power projects where alleged favours, deviation from policies and benefits were drawn by the political leaders, officials and sponsors.

- The Federal Investigation Agency has arrested former National Assembly member Chaudhry Akhtar Vario and two directors of the Tawakkul group of industries in connection with various criminal cases registered against them.
